title: The Seventy - Called and Set Apart

blocks.text: The second circle is the seventy - {{lk 10:1,lk 10:2,lk 10:3,lk 10:4,lk 10:5,lk 10:6,lk 10:7,lk 10:8,lk 10:9,lk 10:10,lk 10:11|Luke 10:1-11}}. They were fully instructed on what to do, how to begin, how to behave, and what to say. Unlike the crowd around them, they weren't bench-warmers - God saw something in them worth setting apart: usefulness, obedience, a willingness to take instruction.

Moving from being an ordinary member (the five hundred) into the workers (the seventy) changes your relationship with the Pastor. As one of the five hundred, you can travel whenever and wherever you like without needing to inform anyone. Once you join the workers, even a weekend visit to see someone requires informing the Pastor first. And if there's a task requiring the presence of every worker that clashes with your own plans, you have to choose - the work, or your own agenda. Once you take up this calling, you're expected to remain in it for good; you may step back voluntarily, but having been made a head, you shouldn't willingly become a tail again.

Those among the seventy learn to serve continuously and without supervision. When Jesus sent them out, He didn't accompany them Himself - meaning each of them had to perform well whether or not anyone was watching, because ultimately, they weren't working for man but for God, who alone rewards them - {{ph 2:12|Philippians 2:12}}; {{cl 3:22,cl 3:23,cl 3:24|Colossians 3:22-24}}.

Jesus also asked them to travel without money, to teach them endurance and dependence. Fasting is one of the responsibilities that comes with this calling - there will be days at church with no time to eat until evening, and enduring that builds spiritual growth. Whatever you have, you're expected to use for God, giving your very best - {{mt 5:20,mt 5:21,mt 5:22,mt 5:23|Matthew 5:20-23}}; {{mk 14:3,mk 14:4,mk 14:5,mk 14:6,mk 14:7,mk 14:8,mk 14:9|Mark 14:3-9}}.

Serving without supervision also means serving without seeking recognition - working joyfully and humbly, without the need to be seen or praised - {{1pe 4:11|1 Peter 4:11}}; {{jo 13:14|John 13:14}}; {{ps 100:2|Psalm 100:2}}. And finally, remember that none of it is wasted effort - {{1co 15:58|1 Corinthians 15:58}}.

cards.heading: What is asked of the seventy

blocks.text: In summary, those in the group of the seventy must:

items: Be willing to work to the best of their ability.
Be willing to use whatever they have, and their very best, for God.
Learn to serve without seeking anyone's praise, giving all glory to God.
Be willing to serve with joy.
Constantly remember that their efforts will not be in vain.
Know that they need prayer to make all of the above possible - {{jo 15:5|John 15:5}}; "without me you can do nothing" - {{mk 3:13,mk 3:14,mk 3:15|Mark 3:13-15}}.
